decisions.choice: authority: the legal right and power to decide
decisions.reason: The word means the right to act, and the power that goes with it. As the Roman governor of Judea, Pilate held the power of life and death over a prisoner like Jesus (18:31). John uses the same word for the authority the Father gave the Son (5:27; 10:18; 17:2), and Jesus takes it up in his reply.

decisions.choice: release ... crucify (SBLGNT)
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts put the two the other way round: "to crucify you, and ... to release you". The older manuscripts have the order given here. The sense is the same. A reviewer should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: Do you not know: a question that expects the answer yes
decisions.reason: The negative form expects agreement: surely you know this. Pilate means it as a warning.

decisions.choice: power (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says "power", the everyday word, here and in verse 11, so that Jesus's reply is heard as an answer to Pilate's claim. Literal and Balanced keep "authority" (meaning decision m1). Readable says "have you crucified", since the governor's soldiers would carry it out.

decisions.choice: poder (R); autoridad (L, B); hacer que te crucifiquen (R)
decisions.reason: As in English: Readable uses the everyday word here and in verse 11, so that Jesus's reply is heard as an answer to Pilate's claim (meaning decision m1), and says "hacer que te crucifiquen" since his soldiers would carry it out.

The word is the legal right to decide, with the power that goes with it (m1). 権限 is the word for an official's legal power; 権威 would sound like moral or spiritual authority. Readable says 力, as the English Readable says power. The sentence has no quotation marks because the English continues Pilate's speech without them; the Japanese follows the English marks.

records.literal_gloss: Answered him Jesus, "Not you would have authority against me none, if not it was given to you from above; because of this the [one] having handed over me to you greater sin has."

en.L: Jesus answered him, "You would have no authority over {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} at all if it had not been given to you from above; because of this the one who handed {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} over to you has [the] greater sin."
en.B: Jesus answered, "You would have no authority over {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} at all unless it had been given to you from above. That is why the one who handed {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} over to you carries the greater sin."
en.R: Jesus answered, "You would not have any power over {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} if God had not given it to you. So the person who handed {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} over to you is even more guilty of sin than you are."

es.L: Le respondió Jesús: «No tendrías ninguna autoridad sobre {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} si no te hubiera sido dado desde arriba; por eso el que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} entregó a ti tiene mayor pecado».
es.B: Jesús le respondió: «No tendrías ninguna autoridad sobre {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} si no se te hubiera dado desde arriba. Por eso, el que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} entregó a ti carga con un pecado mayor».
es.R: Jesús le respondió: «No tendrías ningún poder sobre {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} si Dios no te lo hubiera dado. Por eso, el que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} entregó a ti es todavía más culpable que tú».

fr.B: Jésus répondit : « Tu n’aurais aucune autorité sur {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} si cela ne t’avait pas été donné d’en haut. C’est pourquoi celui qui {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}a livré à toi porte un plus grand péché. »
fr.R: Jésus a répondu : « Tu n’aurais aucun pouvoir sur {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} si Dieu ne te l’avait pas donné. C’est pourquoi celui qui {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}a livré à toi a commis un péché encore plus grave que le tien. »

vi.B: Đức Giê-xu đáp: "Ông chẳng có quyền gì trên {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} cả, nếu không phải từ trên cao ban cho ông. Vì thế, kẻ đã nộp {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} cho ông mang tội nặng hơn."

pt.B: Jesus respondeu: "Você não teria autoridade nenhuma sobre {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}} se isso não lhe tivesse sido dado do alto. Por isso, aquele que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} entregou a você carrega um pecado maior."

am.L: ኢየሱስ እንዲህ ብሎ መለሰለት፦ «ከላይ ባይሰጥህ ኖሮ በእኔ ላይ ምንም ሥልጣን ባልኖረህ ነበር፤ ስለዚህ ለአንተ አሳልፎ የሰጠኝ የሚበልጥ ኃጢአት አለበት።»

id.R: Yesus menjawab, "Kamu tidak akan mempunyai kuasa apa pun atas diri-{{deity_pronoun:ku|Ku}} kalau Allah tidak memberikannya kepadamu. Jadi orang yang menyerahkan {{deity_pronoun:aku|Aku}} kepadamu lebih bersalah daripada kamu."

decisions.choice: from above: from God
decisions.reason: John uses this word for what comes from God and from heaven (3:3, 31); compare 3:27, "unless it has been given him from heaven". Pilate's power over Jesus comes from God, not finally from the emperor, and it is given only for this hour.

decisions.choice: it had been given: the whole matter, not only the word "authority"
alternatives: the authority itself had been given
decisions.reason: The participle is neuter, while the word for authority is feminine. So "it" most likely means the whole situation, Pilate's power over Jesus at this moment, which God has allowed. The sense is the same as if authority alone were meant.

decisions.choice: because of this ... the greater sin: Pilate is guilty, but the one who handed Jesus over is more guilty
alternatives: Pilate has no sin at all
decisions.reason: Pilate acts with a power that God has given to his office, though he is still responsible for how he uses it; "greater" means that Pilate's sin is real too. The one who handed Jesus over did so knowingly, from his own will, and set the whole matter in motion. Jesus speaks of guilt in this one case, not of any group or people.

decisions.choice: the one who handed me over to you: most likely Caiaphas, the high priest
alternatives: the chief priests as a group
decisions.reason: The word is singular. Caiaphas sent Jesus to Pilate (18:24, 28) and had said that one man should die for the nation (11:49-50; 18:14), and Pilate has said, "Your nation and the chief priests handed you over to me" (18:35). Others take it to mean Judas, whom John often calls the one who handed Jesus over (6:64, 71; 13:11; 18:2, 5); but Judas handed him over to the men sent by the chief priests (18:3), not to Pilate. Either way it names a single person who acted, not a people.

decisions.choice: if God had not given it to you (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly who is meant by "from above" (meaning decision m1) and uses "power" as in verse 10.

decisions.choice: carries the greater sin (B); is even more guilty of sin than you are (R)
decisions.reason: To "have sin" is a way of speaking of guilt, as in 9:41 and 15:22, 24. Readable says "even more ... than you are" to show that Pilate's own guilt is real (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: dado (masculine form, neuter sense), not dada
alternatives: si no te hubiera sido dada
decisions.reason: Spanish can show what meaning decision m2 finds: "si no te hubiera sido dado" (L), "se te hubiera dado" (B) and "te lo hubiera dado" (R) refer to the whole matter, not to the feminine "autoridad".

decisions.choice: si Dios no te lo hubiera dado; es todavía más culpable que tú (R)
decisions.reason: As in English: Readable says who is meant by "from above" (meaning decision m1), and "más culpable que tú" shows that Pilate's own guilt is real (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: si cela ne t'avait pas été donné
alternatives: si elle ne t'avait pas été donnée
decisions.reason: The Greek participle is neuter while the word for authority is feminine, so "it" most likely means the whole matter (meaning decision m2). French "autorité" is feminine too, and "elle" would tie the clause to the word; the neuter "cela" keeps the Greek openness.

decisions.choice: a commis un péché encore plus grave que le tien (R)
alternatives: est encore plus coupable que toi
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the word "péché" and shows, with "que le tien", that Pilate's own sin is real (meaning decision m3), as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: kukabidhi (hand over)
decisions.reason: The same verb runs through the story: Judas, the chief priests and Pilate each hand Jesus over (meaning decision m4; 19:16). "Kukabidhi" is used for each of them; "kusaliti" (betray) would point to Judas alone and settle a question the meaning note leaves open. "Yeye" here is the one who handed him over, so it carries no reader setting.

decisions.choice: Jesus to Pilate: "ông", himself "Ta"
decisions.reason: As in 18:34: courteous to the official, without deference.

decisions.choice: se isso não lhe tivesse sido dado
alternatives: se ela não lhe tivesse sido dada
decisions.reason: Portuguese, like Greek, marks gender on the participle. The Greek one is neuter, not agreeing with "authority" (meaning decision m2), so Portuguese says "isso ... dado", the whole matter, rather than "ela ... dada", the authority. Readable follows the English in naming God and the power.

decisions.choice: The "if" clause comes first (L, B)
alternatives: Keeping the Greek order, main clause first
decisions.reason: An Amharic condition comes before its main clause, so "you would have no authority ... if it had not been given" becomes "if it had not been given ..., you would have no authority"; the meaning is unchanged.

decisions.choice: "परमेश्वर ने" (R)
decisions.reason: "From above" means from God (meaning decision m1); Readable names him, as the English Readable does, while Literal and Balanced keep "ऊपर से".

decisions.choice: "если бы не было дано" (L)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the neuter of the Greek, which speaks of the whole matter as given, not only of the power (meaning decision m2); Balanced and Readable make "власть" the subject, as Russian prefers.

decisions.choice: "上から" (L, B), "神が与えられた" (R); "引き渡した者" at every level
decisions.reason: From above means from God (m1); Literal and Balanced keep "上から" so that the link with 3:3 and 3:31 stays, and Readable names God. The one who handed Jesus over is most likely Caiaphas (m4), not Judas, so the general "引き渡す" stands at every level rather than the "裏切る" used of Judas at Balanced and Readable.

decisions.choice: Jesus answers Pilate in the plain style and calls him "あなた"
decisions.reason: As in 18:34-37: Jesus does not plead before the governor; the plain style keeps his calm authority, and あなた, not おまえ, keeps it from sounding rude.

source.text: ἐκ τούτου ὁ Πιλᾶτος ἐζήτει ἀπολῦσαι αὐτόν· οἱ δὲ Ἰουδαῖοι ἐκραύγασαν λέγοντες· Ἐὰν τοῦτον ἀπολύσῃς, οὐκ εἶ φίλος τοῦ Καίσαρος· πᾶς ὁ βασιλέα ἑαυτὸν ποιῶν ἀντιλέγει τῷ Καίσαρι.

records.literal_gloss: From this the Pilate was seeking to release him; but the Jews cried out saying, "If this [man] you release, not you are friend of the Caesar; everyone the king himself making speaks against the Caesar."

en.L: From this [time] Pilate was seeking to release {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, but the Jews shouted, saying, "If you release this [man], you are not a friend of Caesar; everyone who makes himself a king speaks against Caesar."
en.B: From then on Pilate tried to set {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} free, but the Jewish leaders shouted, "If you let this man go, you are no friend of Caesar. Anyone who claims to be a king is setting himself against Caesar."
en.R: After this, Pilate kept trying to find a way to let Jesus go. But the Jewish leaders shouted, "If you let this man go, you are not Caesar's friend! Anyone who says he is a king is an enemy of Caesar, the emperor!"

es.L: Desde este [momento] Pilato procuraba soltarlo; pero los judíos gritaron diciendo: «Si sueltas a este, no eres amigo de César; todo el que se hace rey habla contra César».
es.B: Desde entonces Pilato trató de dejarlo en libertad, pero los dirigentes judíos gritaron: «Si dejas ir a este hombre, no eres amigo de César. Cualquiera que pretende ser rey se pone en contra de César».
es.R: Después de esto, Pilato siguió buscando la manera de dejar ir a Jesús. Pero los dirigentes judíos gritaron: «¡Si dejas ir a este hombre, no eres amigo de César! ¡Cualquiera que dice que es rey es enemigo de César, el emperador!».

fr.L: Dès lors Pilate cherchait à {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} relâcher ; mais les Juifs crièrent, en disant : « Si tu relâches celui-ci, tu n’es pas ami de César ; quiconque se fait roi se déclare contre César. »
fr.B: Dès lors, Pilate cherchait à {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} libérer ; mais les chefs juifs crièrent : « Si tu laisses partir cet homme, tu n’es pas un ami de César. Quiconque se prétend roi se dresse contre César. »
fr.R: Après cela, Pilate cherchait sans cesse un moyen de laisser partir Jésus. Mais les chefs juifs ont crié : « Si tu laisses partir cet homme, tu n’es pas l’ami de César ! Celui qui dit qu’il est roi est un ennemi de César, l’empereur ! »

sw.L: Tangu hapo Pilato alikuwa akitafuta kumwachilia; lakini Wayahudi walipiga kelele, wakisema, "Ukimwachilia huyu, wewe si rafiki wa Kaisari; kila mtu anayejifanya mfalme anampinga Kaisari."
sw.B: Tangu wakati huo Pilato alijaribu kumwachilia huru, lakini viongozi wa Wayahudi wakapiga kelele, "Ukimwacha mtu huyu aende, wewe si rafiki wa Kaisari. Yeyote anayejidai kuwa mfalme anajiweka kinyume cha Kaisari."
sw.R: Baada ya hayo, Pilato aliendelea kutafuta njia ya kumwachilia Yesu. Lakini viongozi wa Wayahudi walipiga kelele, "Ukimwacha mtu huyu aende, wewe si rafiki wa Kaisari! Mtu yeyote anayesema kwamba yeye ni mfalme ni adui wa Kaisari, mtawala mkuu wa Roma!"

vi.L: Từ [lúc] đó, Phi-lát tìm cách tha {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, nhưng người Do Thái la lên rằng: "Nếu quan tha người này, quan không phải là bạn của Sê-sa. Ai tự xưng mình là vua thì chống lại Sê-sa."
vi.B: Từ lúc đó, Phi-lát tìm cách thả {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, nhưng các nhà lãnh đạo Do Thái la lên: "Nếu quan thả người này, quan không phải là bạn của Sê-sa. Ai tự xưng là vua tức là chống lại Sê-sa."
vi.R: Từ đó, Phi-lát cứ tìm cách thả Đức Giê-xu. Nhưng các nhà lãnh đạo Do Thái la lên: "Nếu quan thả người này thì quan không phải là bạn của Sê-sa! Ai tự xưng là vua đều là kẻ thù của Sê-sa, tức là hoàng đế!"

ko.L: 이때부터 빌라도는 그분을 놓아주려고 애썼다. 그러나 유대인들이 소리 지르며 말했다. "이 [사람]을 놓아주시면 [총독님은] 가이사의 친구가 아닙니다. 자기를 왕으로 삼는 사람은 누구나 가이사를 거슬러 말하는 것입니다."
ko.B: 이때부터 빌라도는 예수를 놓아주려고 애썼다. 그러나 유대 지도자들이 소리를 질렀다. "이 사람을 놓아주시면 총독님은 가이사의 친구가 아닙니다. 자기를 왕이라고 하는 사람은 누구나 가이사에게 맞서는 것입니다."
ko.R: 그 뒤로 빌라도는 예수를 풀어 줄 방법을 계속 찾았다. 그러나 유대 지도자들이 소리쳤다. "이 사람을 놓아주시면 총독님은 황제의 친구가 아닙니다! 자기가 왕이라고 하는 사람은 누구나 로마 황제 가이사의 원수입니다!"

pt.L: Desde então, Pilatos procurava soltá-{{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}}, mas os judeus gritaram, dizendo: "Se o senhor soltar este [homem], o senhor não é amigo de César; todo aquele que se faz rei se opõe a César."
pt.B: Daí em diante, Pilatos tentava soltá-{{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}}, mas os líderes judeus gritaram: "Se o senhor soltar este homem, o senhor não é amigo de César. Quem se declara rei está se colocando contra César."
pt.R: Depois disso, Pilatos continuou procurando um jeito de soltar Jesus. Mas os líderes judeus gritaram: "Se o senhor soltar esse homem, o senhor não é amigo de César! Quem diz que é rei é inimigo de César, o imperador!"

am.L: ከዚህ [ጊዜ] ጀምሮ ጲላጦስ ሊፈታው ይፈልግ ነበር፤ አይሁድ ግን፦ «ይህን [ሰው] ቢፈቱ የቄሳር ወዳጅ አይደሉም፤ ራሱን ንጉሥ የሚያደርግ ሁሉ ቄሳርን ይቃወማል» እያሉ ጮኹ።
am.B: ከዚያን ጊዜ ጀምሮ ጲላጦስ ሊፈታው ሞከረ፤ የአይሁድ መሪዎች ግን፦ «ይህን ሰው ቢለቁት የቄሳር ወዳጅ አይደሉም። ንጉሥ ነኝ የሚል ሁሉ ቄሳርን ይቃወማል» እያሉ ጮኹ።
am.R: ከዚህ በኋላ ጲላጦስ ኢየሱስን የሚለቅበትን መንገድ ይፈልግ ነበር። የአይሁድ መሪዎች ግን፦ «ይህን ሰው ቢለቁት የቄሳር ወዳጅ አይደሉም! ንጉሥ ነኝ የሚል ሁሉ የንጉሠ ነገሥቱ የቄሳር ጠላት ነው!» እያሉ ጮኹ።

hi.L: इस पर पिलातुस उन्हें छोड़ देना चाहता था, पर यहूदी चिल्लाकर कहने लगे, "यदि आप इसे छोड़ देंगे, तो आप कैसर के मित्र नहीं हैं; जो कोई अपने आप को राजा बनाता है, वह कैसर का विरोध करता है।"
hi.B: तब से पिलातुस उन्हें छोड़ देने का यत्न करता रहा, पर यहूदी अगुवे चिल्लाए, "यदि आप इस मनुष्य को छोड़ देंगे, तो आप कैसर के मित्र नहीं हैं। जो कोई राजा होने का दावा करता है, वह कैसर का विरोधी है।"
hi.R: इसके बाद पिलातुस यीशु को छोड़ने का रास्ता ढूँढ़ता रहा। पर यहूदी अगुवे चिल्लाए, "अगर आप इस आदमी को छोड़ देंगे, तो आप कैसर के मित्र नहीं हैं! जो कोई कहता है कि वह राजा है, वह कैसर, यानी सम्राट, का दुश्मन है!"

ru.L: С этого [времени] Пилат искал, как отпустить {{deity_pronoun:его|Его}}; иудеи же кричали, говоря: «Если отпустишь этого, ты не друг кесарю; всякий, делающий себя царём, противится кесарю.»
ru.B: С тех пор Пилат старался освободить {{deity_pronoun:его|Его}}, но иудейские власти кричали: «Если отпустишь этого человека, ты не друг кесарю. Всякий, кто называет себя царём, восстаёт против кесаря.»
ru.R: После этого Пилат всё пытался найти способ отпустить Иисуса. Но иудейские вожди кричали: «Если ты отпустишь этого человека, ты не друг кесарю! Кто называет себя царём, тот враг кесаря, римского императора!»

uk.L: Відтоді Пилат шукав, [як] відпустити {{deity_pronoun:його|Його}}, а юдеї закричали, кажучи: «Якщо відпустиш цього, ти не друг кесаря; кожен, хто робить себе царем, виступає проти кесаря.»
uk.B: Відтоді Пилат намагався звільнити {{deity_pronoun:його|Його}}, але представники юдейської влади кричали: «Якщо відпустиш цього чоловіка, ти не друг кесаря. Кожен, хто видає себе за царя, повстає проти кесаря.»
uk.R: Після цього Пилат усе шукав способу відпустити Ісуса. Але юдейські провідники кричали: «Якщо ти відпустиш цього чоловіка, то ти не друг кесаря! Кожен, хто називає себе царем, — ворог кесаря, імператора!»

ja.L: このことから、ピラトはイエスを釈放しようと努めていた。しかしユダヤ人たちは叫んで言った。「もしこの[者]を釈放するなら、あなたは皇帝の友ではありません。自分を王とする者はみな、皇帝に逆らっているのです。」
ja.B: そのときから、ピラトはイエスを釈放しようと努めた。しかし、ユダヤ人の指導者たちは叫んだ。「その男を釈放するなら、あなたは皇帝の友ではありません。自分を王だと言う者はだれでも、皇帝に背いているのです。」
ja.R: その後、ピラトは、イエスを放す方法をなんとか見つけようとしました。しかし、ユダヤ人の指導者たちは叫びました。「その男を放すなら、総督は皇帝の友ではなくなります！自分は王だと言う者はみな、ローマ皇帝の敵です！」

id.L: Sejak itu Pilatus berusaha membebaskan {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}}, tetapi orang-orang Yahudi berteriak, katanya, "Jika engkau membebaskan orang ini, engkau bukan sahabat Kaisar; setiap orang yang menjadikan dirinya raja, ia melawan Kaisar."
id.B: Sejak itu Pilatus berusaha membebaskan {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}}, tetapi para pemimpin Yahudi berteriak, "Kalau engkau membebaskan orang ini, engkau bukan sahabat Kaisar. Siapa pun yang mengaku dirinya raja, ia melawan Kaisar."
id.R: Sesudah itu Pilatus terus mencari jalan untuk membebaskan Yesus. Tetapi para pemimpin Yahudi berteriak, "Kalau engkau membebaskan orang ini, engkau bukan sahabat Kaisar! Siapa saja yang mengaku dirinya raja adalah musuh Kaisar, sang kaisar Romawi!"

decisions.choice: from this: from then on, and because of what Jesus had said
decisions.reason: The phrase can mark time ("from then on") or a reason ("because of this"); John uses it the same way in 6:66, where both senses are possible. Here Jesus's answer is the turning point, so both fit.

decisions.choice: was seeking: kept trying
decisions.reason: The imperfect shows repeated or continued attempts. Pilate kept looking for a way to release Jesus, without success.

decisions.choice: the Jews: the chief priests and their officers, with those who stood with them outside the praetorium
decisions.reason: They are the accusers of verses 6-7, who answer Pilate again; in verse 15 John names the chief priests as the ones who speak for them. Others may have stood with them, as the shout for Barabbas suggests (18:39-40), but John does not describe a crowd. It is not the Jewish people as a whole: Jesus and his disciples are Jews.

decisions.choice: Caesar's friend: loyal to the emperor, perhaps also an honored title
decisions.reason: "Caesar" here means the Roman emperor, Tiberius at this time (Luke 3:1). "Friend of Caesar" means one loyal to him; it was also used of men honored with the emperor's favor, but whether Pilate held such a title is not known. The threat is plain: if he releases a man accused of claiming to be king, they will report him as disloyal.

decisions.choice: makes himself a king speaks against Caesar: claims to be a king and so opposes the emperor
decisions.reason: The verb means to speak against and so to oppose; to set oneself up as a king in a Roman province was rebellion. "Makes himself a king" repeats the form of the charge in verse 7, "made himself the Son of God": the accusers now turn the religious charge into a political one.

decisions.choice: the Jewish leaders
decisions.reason: Where the word means the authorities, Balanced and Readable name them (see the book's terms). The footnote gives the word John wrote.

decisions.choice: Caesar, the emperor (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says who Caesar was, the first time the name comes in the passage (meaning decision m4), and says "enemy of" for "speaks against" (meaning decision m5).

decisions.choice: los dirigentes judíos
decisions.reason: As in verse 7: the accusers of verses 6-7 (meaning decision m3). The footnote gives the word John wrote.

decisions.choice: César, el emperador (R)
decisions.reason: As in English: Readable says who Caesar was the first time the name comes (meaning decision m4), and says "enemigo de" for "speaks against" (meaning decision m5).

decisions.choice: Dès lors (L, B); Après cela (R)
decisions.reason: The phrase can mark time or a reason, and both fit here (meaning decision m1). French "dès lors" means both "from then on" and "for that reason", so Literal and Balanced keep the double sense; Readable uses the plain time phrase.

decisions.choice: the accusers to Pilate: "quan"
decisions.reason: As in 18:30: "quan" is how subjects address an official; "ngài" is kept for the deity pronoun.

decisions.choice: the accusers' argument in 합쇼체, with "[총독님은]" (L) / "총독님은" (B, R) for "you"
decisions.reason: As in 18:30: Korean does not call a superior "you", and the threat is put as an argument, not a shout, so it keeps the polite level.

decisions.choice: "ቢፈቱ", "አይደሉም" (if you release, you are not): the respectful form to Pilate
decisions.reason: As in 18:30, the Jewish leaders speak to the governor as subjects to a ruler. The respect of the form is on the surface only; the words are a threat.

decisions.choice: "иудейские власти" (B); "иудейские вожди" (R)
decisions.reason: The chief priests and those with them are meant (meaning decision m3); Literal keeps "иудеи".

decisions.choice: "кесарь"
decisions.reason: The traditional Russian Bible word for the emperor (style guide); Readable adds who he was, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "皇帝" (every level; also 19:15); "ローマ皇帝" once (R)
decisions.reason: Caesar here is the Roman emperor (m4), a title rather than a personal name; "皇帝" says so at every level, as Acts does. Readable adds "ローマ" once, as the English Readable adds "the emperor".

decisions.choice: the leaders keep the polite style to Pilate ("ありません", "のです"); "あなた" (L, B), "総督" (R)
decisions.reason: They threaten the governor but still address him as subjects; as in 18:30, Readable uses his title in place of あなた. Their cry for Barabbas (18:40) and their shouts at the prisoner are plain because they are not addressed to Pilate.

decisions.choice: sat down: Pilate took his seat
alternatives: Pilate seated Jesus on the judgment seat
decisions.reason: The verb usually means "sat" in John (12:14), and a governor sat on the judgment seat to give sentence (Matthew 27:19; Acts 25:6, 17). The verb can also mean "seated someone", and the sentence could then mean that Pilate set Jesus on the judgment seat in mockery, as the soldiers had dressed him as a king. That would fit John's irony, but without an object stated the plain sense is more likely.

decisions.choice: judgment seat: the raised platform where a Roman official sat to give his decision
decisions.reason: The word means a platform reached by steps. A Roman magistrate gave judgment from it in public (Acts 18:12; 25:6). By sitting there Pilate makes his decision formal.

decisions.choice: the Stone Pavement, in Hebrew Gabbatha: two names for the same place
decisions.reason: The first name means a floor laid with stones. "In Hebrew" means the language of the Jews of the land, which in daily speech was mostly Aramaic (as at 5:2). Gabbatha is not a translation of the first name; its meaning is uncertain, perhaps "height" or "raised place". The exact place in Jerusalem is not known.

decisions.choice: these words: the threat of verse 12
decisions.reason: It is the warning that he would be no friend of Caesar that moves Pilate to act.

decisions.choice: in Hebrew
decisions.reason: Keeps the word John used, as at 5:2; meaning decision m3 explains which language this was.

decisions.choice: the judge's seat (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says what the seat was for (meaning decision m2) and breaks the long sentence.

decisions.choice: tribunal (L, B); el asiento del juez (R)
decisions.reason: Spanish "tribunal" names both a court and the raised seat from which a judge gives sentence (meaning decision m2); Readable says plainly what the seat was for.

decisions.choice: el Enlosado; en hebreo Gabatá
decisions.reason: "Enlosado" is a floor laid with stone slabs, the meaning of the first name (meaning decision m3). "En hebreo" keeps the word John used, as at 5:2.

decisions.choice: le tribunal (L, B); le siège du juge (R); le Dallage
decisions.reason: In French Bibles "tribunal" names the raised seat from which a Roman magistrate gave judgment (meaning decision m2), but today it mostly means a court of law, so Readable says what the seat was for. "Dallage" is a floor laid with flagstones, the meaning of the Greek name (meaning decision m3); it is written with a capital as a place name.

decisions.choice: "Nền Lát Đá"; "tiếng Hê-bơ-rơ"
decisions.reason: The place name is translated as a name, capitalised. "tiếng Hê-bơ-rơ" follows John's word and the Protestant spelling; the language spoken was probably Aramaic, as the English notes say.

decisions.choice: "돌을 깐 뜰" (L, B); "돌을 깔아 놓은 뜰" (R); "히브리 말" for Hebraisti
decisions.reason: The Greek name describes a stone-paved court; the older Sino-Korean term "박석" is unfamiliar today. "히브리 말" follows John's own word; what language he means is left to a note, as in English.

decisions.choice: o tribunal (L, B); a cadeira de juiz (R); Gabatá
decisions.reason: "Tribunal" is the Portuguese word for the raised seat from which a Roman magistrate gave sentence, as well as for the court (meaning decision m2); Readable says plainly what it was. The Aramaic name is spelled as Portuguese writes its sounds, "Gabatá", like "Gólgota" in verse 17.

decisions.choice: "የፍርድ ወንበር" (judgment seat, L, B), "የዳኛ ወንበር" (R); "የድንጋይ ንጣፍ" (the Stone Pavement); "በዕብራይስጥ ገበታ" (in Hebrew Gabbatha)
alternatives: "ጋባታ" (a closer copy of the Greek letters)
decisions.reason: "የፍርድ ወንበር" is Matthew 27:19's word. The place name is translated, and its Hebrew name is given in the form Amharic readers know; Literal brackets the words Amharic needs to finish the sentence.

decisions.choice: "Каменный помост", "по-еврейски Гаввафа"
decisions.reason: The Greek name is translated, as the English does, and the Hebrew name keeps its traditional Russian form. "По-еврейски" keeps the word John used, as at 5:2; the meaning decision says which language it was.

decisions.choice: "судилище" (L, B), "суддівське місце" (R); "Камʼяний Поміст" for the Greek name
decisions.reason: "Судилище" is the term settled in the letters for the judgment seat; the Greek place name is translated, as John's reader understood it, beside the Semitic name Gabbatha.

decisions.choice: "裁きの座" (L, B), "裁判をする人の席" (R); "石畳" and "ガバタ"
decisions.reason: The judgment seat is the platform from which a Roman official gave his decision (m2), and Pilate takes his seat on it (m1). The first name of the place means a stone-paved floor (m3), so Japanese translates it as 石畳 and transliterates the Hebrew (Aramaic) name, with ヘブライ語 as at 5:2.

decisions.choice: "Lantai Batu"; "Gabata"
decisions.reason: m3: two names for the same place. John translates the Greek name, so Indonesian translates it too ("Lantai Batu"), and keeps the Hebrew name in the brief's spelling (Style, section 6, rule 4); added to docs/indonesian-terms.md.

decisions.choice: the Preparation of the Passover: the day before the Passover, when the meal was made ready
alternatives: the Friday of the Passover week
decisions.reason: On the day of preparation the Passover lambs were killed in the afternoon (Exodus 12:6) and the meal was eaten that evening, when the feast began. This fits 18:28, where the accusers have not yet eaten the Passover. The same word was also the name for Friday, the day of preparation before the Sabbath (19:31, 42; Mark 15:42), and some read it here as "the Friday of Passover week". Mark 14:12-16 presents the last supper as a Passover meal, so the two accounts need to be read together; the footnote gives the other reading.

decisions.choice: about the sixth hour: about noon
alternatives: about six in the morning, counting from midnight
decisions.reason: Hours were counted from sunrise, about six in the morning (see the notes at 1:39 and 4:6), so the sixth hour was about midday. Mark 15:25 says Jesus was crucified at the third hour, about nine in the morning. Times of day were usually given loosely ("about"). Counting from midnight, which some have proposed for John, would give six in the morning. The difference is noted here, not settled.

decisions.choice: noon on the day of preparation: perhaps a link with the Passover lambs
alternatives: the time is given only as a fact
decisions.reason: At about this hour the preparations for killing the Passover lambs were beginning. John has called Jesus the Lamb of God (1:29, 36), and he will connect the Passover lamb with Jesus's death (19:36; Exodus 12:46). He does not draw the link here, so it is possible rather than certain.

decisions.choice: about the sixth hour (Literal); about noon (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The book-wide choice for clock times in John: Literal keeps the hour as counted then, Balanced and Readable give the modern time (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: the day of Preparation (B, R); when people got ready for the Passover (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable supply "day". Readable says what the day was for (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: como la hora sexta (L); cerca del mediodía (B, R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide choice for clock times, as at 4:6: Literal keeps the hour as counted then, Balanced and Readable give the modern time (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: el día de la Preparación (B, R); cuando la gente lo dejaba todo listo para la fiesta de la Pascua (R)
decisions.reason: As in English: Balanced and Readable supply "día", and Readable says what the day was for (meaning decision m1). "Preparación" has a capital as the name of the day.

decisions.choice: environ la sixième heure (L); vers midi (B); environ midi (R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide choice for clock times in John: Literal keeps the hour as counted from sunrise, Balanced and Readable give the modern time (meaning decision m2). "Midi" is how French says twelve o'clock in speech and writing alike.

decisions.choice: saa sita at every level; mchana added at Balanced and Readable
alternatives: saa sita mchana (B, R) converted as the English "noon"
decisions.reason: The Greek counts hours from sunrise, as Swahili time does, so the sixth hour is simply "saa sita", midday (meaning decision m2). No conversion is needed, unlike the English "about noon"; Balanced and Readable add "mchana" (daytime) to make it plain.

decisions.choice: Maandalio (L); Siku ya Maandalio (B, R)
decisions.reason: The name of the day before the Passover (meaning decision m1), and of the day before the Sabbath in 19:31, 42, so one word serves both. Balanced and Readable supply "Siku ya" as the English supplies "day".

decisions.choice: "ngày Chuẩn Bị", capitalised as the name of a day
decisions.reason: "ngày sắm sửa" is the old Protestant wording; "ngày Chuẩn Bị" is current Vietnamese for the same thing and reads as the day's name. Used again in 19:31 and 19:42.

decisions.choice: "여섯째 시쯤" (L); "낮 열두 시쯤" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Clock time as the style guide sets it (section 5): Literal keeps the Greek count, Balanced and Readable give the modern time.

decisions.choice: "ስድስተኛው ሰዓት" (the sixth hour, L); "ከቀኑ ስድስት ሰዓት" (B, R), Readable adding "እኩለ ቀን" (noon)
decisions.reason: Ethiopians count the hours of the day from dawn, as the Greek does, so "ከቀኑ ስድስት ሰዓት" is the same time as the Greek's sixth hour and is noon; Readable names it as noon as well.

decisions.choice: "लगभग छठा घंटा" (L); "लगभग दोपहर के बारह बजे" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek count of hours from sunrise; Balanced and Readable give the time as a modern reader counts it (meaning decision m2), as the style guide sets for clock time (section 5).

decisions.choice: "около шестого часа" (L); "около полудня" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Clock times in John: Literal keeps the Greek count, Balanced and Readable give the time as a modern reader counts it (style guide, section 5).

decisions.choice: "близько шостої [години]" (L); "близько полудня" (B, R); "Приготування" (L), "день Приготування" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The clock-time and Preparation conventions settled for the Gospels: Literal keeps the Greek count of hours from sunrise; Balanced and Readable give the time as a modern reader counts it.

decisions.choice: "およそ第六の時" (L); "昼の十二時ごろ" (B, R); "過越祭の準備の日"
decisions.reason: The sixth hour, counted from sunrise, is about noon (m2); Literal keeps the Greek count and Balanced and Readable give the modern time, as at 4:6. The Preparation is the day before the Passover meal (m1), said as 準備の日, and Readable explains it as the day for getting ready.

decisions.choice: "hari Persiapan"; "jam keenam" (L), "pukul dua belas siang" (B, R)
decisions.reason: m1: the day before the Passover. The clock follows the rule of 1:39 and 4:6.

decisions.choice: take away: remove him, that is, put him to death
alternatives: take him out of our sight
decisions.reason: The verb means to lift up and carry off. Shouted at a prisoner, it demands his removal by death, as in Luke 23:18 and Acts 22:22. The cry is doubled, as "Crucify, crucify" was in verse 6.

decisions.choice: those men: the ones Pilate has just addressed
decisions.reason: The pronoun points back to those of verse 14, and the next sentence names the chief priests as their spokesmen.

decisions.choice: Take [him] away (L); Away with him (B)
decisions.reason: Literal brackets "him", which the Greek leaves unstated; Balanced uses the English idiom for demanding someone's removal. Readable says "Take him away".

decisions.choice: llévatelo (L, R); quítalo de en medio (B)
decisions.reason: The verb means to lift up and carry off, here a demand for his death (meaning decision m1). The command is to Pilate, so it is singular and takes no setting. "Quitar de en medio" is the Spanish idiom for getting rid of someone. Spanish joins the object pronoun to the command, so Literal does not bracket it.

decisions.choice: Emporte-[le] (L); Qu'on l'emmène ! (B); Emmène-le ! (R)
decisions.reason: The verb means to lift up and carry off; shouted at a prisoner, it demands his removal by death (meaning decision m1). Literal keeps the picture with "emporter" and brackets the pronoun the Greek leaves unstated; Balanced uses the impersonal "qu'on", a natural French shout; Readable uses the plain imperative to Pilate. "À mort !" would say outright what the cry only implies.

decisions.choice: "Долой!" (B)
decisions.reason: Balanced uses the Russian cry for demanding someone's removal, as the English Balanced uses "Away with him"; Literal and Readable keep the verb.

decisions.choice: "取り除け" (L); "片づけてしまえ" (B); "連れて行け" (R)
decisions.reason: The cry demands that the prisoner be removed by death (m1). Literal keeps the verb's sense of taking away; Balanced uses the blunt 片づける, which Japanese uses of getting rid of a person; Readable keeps the English Readable's plain "take him away", which the next words explain.

decisions.choice: to them: to the will of the chief priests, while Roman soldiers carried out the sentence
alternatives: handed him to the chief priests, who carried out the crucifixion
decisions.reason: By the grammar, "them" are the last people named, the chief priests (verse 15). Yet the crucifixion was carried out by Roman soldiers (19:23, 32), on the governor's order, and the charge set over the cross was Pilate's (19:19). So the sense is that Pilate gave Jesus up to what they demanded and handed him over for execution; it does not mean the chief priests crucified him themselves. Compare Luke 23:25, "he delivered Jesus over to their will". Every level keeps "to them" as the Greek has it.

decisions.choice: handed over: the same verb used all through the story
decisions.reason: Judas handed Jesus over (18:2, 5), the chief priests handed him over to Pilate (18:30, 35), and Jesus has spoken of the one who handed him over (19:11). Now Pilate, who has said three times that he finds no case against him, hands him over to be crucified. The responsibility for the sentence is the Roman governor's.

decisions.choice: Pilate (B, R); Jesus (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Pilate, since the last speakers were the chief priests. Readable names Jesus. "To them" stays at every level (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: Pilato (B, R); Jesús (R); "a ellos" and the passive at every level
decisions.reason: As in English: Balanced and Readable name Pilate, since the last speakers were the chief priests. Every level keeps "a ellos" and the passive "para que fuera crucificado", which does not say who would carry it out (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: livrer, at every level
decisions.reason: The same verb as for Judas (18:2, 5), the chief priests (18:30, 35) and "celui qui m'a livré" (19:11), so that the chain of handing over ends here with Pilate (meaning decision m2). Readable names Jesus and needs "le" for him in "qu'on le crucifie", which takes the setting.

decisions.choice: "предал" (L); "отдал" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The verb of handing over that runs through the passion (meaning decision m2): Literal keeps "предать", as at 18:30 and 18:35.

decisions.choice: "引き渡した" at every level
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used all through the story for handing Jesus over (m2). Here Pilate is the subject, so the general 引き渡す stands at every level; 裏切る is kept for Judas.
